newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Siemens provides phones for solar summit.
newsitem.headline: Siemens provides phones for solar summit.

text.p: Telecommunications giant Siemens is to provide Zimbabwe with a special cellular telephone service to boost telecommunications at the World Solar Summit in Harare next week, industry officials said on Thursday.

Siemens, which won a controversial Z$200 million (U.S.$19.4 million) tender ahead of Swedish rival Ericsson to set up a cellular telephone service for Zimbabwe's state-owned Posts and Telecommunications Corporation (PTC), will provide more than 200 units for the summit which starts on Monday.
"The equipment is already here and they (Siemens) have started activating their network," said one official who refused to be named.
He said the service was being provided at the request of organisers of the two-day meeting, to be attended by 5,000 delegates -- including 25 world leaders -- from 100 countries.
The decision by Siemens follows an offer last month by a local company, S.T. Masiyiwa Holdings, to provide the conference with a free mobile telephone service.

The government, which last year lost a court battle to the company to protect the PTC's monopoly on provision of cellular telephone services, rejected Masiyiwa's offer saying the company had no licence to operate such a network.
The PTC's cellular telephone tender was mired in controversy this year when Siemens also launched a court battle to overturn an earlier award the corporation had made to Ericsson.
Siemens subsequently won a new tender issued on orders from President Robert Mugabe.
